data.body:
_More from Khopkar · Wart & antiviral agents_

**Class:** Antimitotic plant resins — podophyllin (crude 10–25% resin in tincture of benzoin) and podophyllotoxin (purified active lignan, 0.5% solution / 0.15% cream)

## Mechanism of action
- Bind tubulin → arrest mitosis in metaphase → necrosis of wart tissue

## Indications in dermatology & STI
- External anogenital warts (condylomata acuminata) — podophyllotoxin is the patient-applied form; podophyllin is clinic-applied

## Dose & formulations
- Podophyllotoxin 0.5% solution/0.15% cream: twice daily for 3 days, then 4 days off; up to 4 cycles (patient-applied, ≤10 cm², ≤0.5 mL/day)
- Podophyllin 20–25%: applied by clinician to warts (≤10 cm², ≤0.5 mL), protect surrounding skin with petroleum jelly, wash off after 1–4 h; weekly

## Adverse effects
- Local burning, erosion, ulceration
- Podophyllin systemic toxicity if large amounts are applied or absorbed: nausea, vomiting, neuropathy, bone marrow suppression, coma, death
- Podophyllin causes histological changes that mimic dysplasia (podophyllin effect)

## Contraindications
- Pregnancy (teratogenic, fetal death); mucosal (urethral, vaginal, cervical, anal canal) warts; bleeding or large wart areas

## Pregnancy & lactation
Contraindicated — use cryotherapy or TCA instead.

## Viva points
- Contraindicated in pregnancy
- Podophyllotoxin is safer, patient-applied (3 days on, 4 off)
- Wash off podophyllin after 1–4 h

_Sources: Khopkar ch.20 (Podophyllin); Wolverton 4e ch.43. Facts summarised in our own words; Wolverton followed where books differ._
